$comment: AUTHORITY for what a Semiont client asks again for, and when. A client's live queries answer from a cache (protocol/contract/CACHE-SEMANTICS.md); this table says what each event on the bus, and the reopening of a dropped stream, does to it. `queries` names the live queries: the operation of the registry each one `asks`, or the GET of the gateway's API it `reads` when its answer grows with a document, and what one is kept `per` (a resource, an annotation, a set of filters; absent, the knowledge base has one). `refresh` has a row per trigger: `on` is a channel of protocol/specs/src/bus/registry.json; or `reopened`, the stream open again after a drop (never after a handoff, which misses nothing); or `unreadable`, an event on one of the table's channels that cannot be read. A row `refetches` queries (asks again, keeping the value shown meanwhile), `writes` those whose new value the event itself carries, and `removes` those whose entity the event says is gone, which then fail as `bus.not-found`. `reach` says which keys: `subject`, the resource the event names and, of that resource's annotations, the one it names, or each the client holds when it names none; or `held`, every key the client holds. `names` says where in the event (the frame's payload) a `subject` row finds them: the way to the `resource` (a ResourceId) and to the `annotation` (an AnnotationId), the names of the members it is within and its own joined by dots, as a frame's refusal names a member. `carries` is the way to the value the row `writes` (an Annotation). A way names none where its member, or a member it passes through, is absent or null. A member it passes through that is present and is no object, the member it ends at present and not of its type, and a frame its channel's reading refuses each make the event `unreadable`, whose row applies in its place. `when` splits a channel whose events come two ways: `enriched`, when the member its `enriched` row `carries` is present and not null, and `unenriched` otherwise. packages/codegen/schemas/cache-refresh-table.mjs holds every way to the schema of its channel's events. A client acts only on keys it holds (B20). TypeScript: packages/codegen/schemas/generate-cache-refresh.mjs writes packages/typescript/core/src/generated/cache-refresh.ts. protocol/conformance/sdk builds a live case from every row.

queries.name: events
queries.docs: The recorded history of a resource.

queries.name: referencedBy
queries.docs: The annotations elsewhere that refer to a resource.

queries.name: resources
queries.docs: A list of resources, one per set of filters asked for. It is a query's answer, kept fresh by what every client hears and by the events of the resources whose scope the client holds, and by nothing else: a resource archived, unarchived or retagged elsewhere, by someone else, does not refresh it.

queries.name: matchedResources
queries.docs: The resources a text search found, one per search and set of filters asked for. A query's answer like `resources`, and kept fresh by the same events and no others.

queries.name: engines
queries.docs: The knowledge base's engines, joined with the limits each inference key holder reports: asking again asks every `<flow>:limits-requested` operation of the registry again too.

refresh.docs: The stream is open again after a drop. Events every client hears carry no position, so the ones published meanwhile are lost and nothing replays them: the client asks again for everything they feed. What a resource's own scope feeds needs nothing here: its events are replayed from where the client left off, or `bus:resume-gap` says they could not be.

A frame on a channel of this table that its reading refuses, or one a member of which the row names is present and is not what it names: something changed and nothing says what, so every key held is asked for again, as after a gap.
The gateway could not replay what a scope missed: everything held of that resource, and of its annotations, is asked for again.
An annotation was added to the resource.
An annotation was removed from the resource.
The reply to this client's own deletion: the annotation is gone whether or not the client holds the scope that would tell it so.
An annotation's body changed, and the event carries the annotation as it now is.
An annotation's body changed, and the event could not say what it now is.
An entity tag was added to the resource.
An entity tag was removed from the resource.
The resource was archived, which its description states and lists filter on.
A resource was created as a clone.
A resource was renamed or moved.
An entity type was added to the knowledge base.
A tag schema was added to the knowledge base.
